nodes.summary: The cost of the one-pass relaxation in topological order consists of three natural-number counters: the number of vertices taken from the order, the number of edge occurrences checked for relaxation, and the number of distance installations (strict improvements or first finite distances).
nodes.title: Cost of the DAG shortest-path pass

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and $s$ a source vertex. If the DAG shortest-path algorithm on $E$ from $s$ succeeds, then for every vertex $t$ the returned distance to $t$ is infinite if and only if $t$ is not reachable from $s$ in the directed graph with an edge $u \to v$ for each edge of $E$ from $u$ to $v$.
nodes.title: Unreachable vertices are exactly those at infinite DAG distance

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and $s$ a source vertex. Suppose the DAG shortest-path algorithm on $E$ from $s$ succeeds and returns a finite distance $d \in \mathbb{Z}$ for a vertex $t$. Then some path from $s$ to $t$ in $E$ has weight $d$, and every path from $s$ to $t$ in $E$ has weight at least $d$. Here a path from $s$ to $t$ in $E$ is a list of edges…
nodes.title: DAG shortest-path distances are shortest-path weights

nodes.summary: For a list $E$ of integer-weighted edges on $n$ vertices, a source $s$, and lists $P$ and $R$ of vertices, the DAG shortest-path algorithm on $E$ from $s$ returns the error $(P, R)$ if and only if Kahn's topological sort of the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights fails after processing $P$ and leaving $R$.
nodes.title: Failure output of DAG shortest paths

nodes.title: Successful output of DAG shortest paths

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and $s$ a source vertex. If the DAG shortest-path algorithm on $E$ from $s$ fails, reporting the processed vertices and the list $R$ of remaining vertices of its topological sort, then the directed graph with an edge $u \to v$ for each edge of $E$ from $u$ to $v$ contains a nonempty directed cycle without repeated vertices…
nodes.title: A failed DAG shortest-path run exhibits a cycle

Suppose the DAG shortest-path algorithm on $E$ from $s$ succeeds, and following its predecessor edges back from a vertex $t$ reaches $s$ within $n$ steps, giving the path $P$. nodes.title: Extracted DAG shortest paths are shortest paths

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and $s$ a source vertex. The DAG shortest-path algorithm on $E$ from $s$ succeeds if and only if the directed graph with an edge $u \to v$ for each edge of $E$ from $u$ to $v$ has no directed cycle.
nodes.title: The DAG shortest-path algorithm succeeds exactly on acyclic graphs

If it succeeds with order $\sigma$, start from distance $0$ at $s$ and $\infty$ elsewhere, relax the outgoing edge occurrences of each vertex in the order $\sigma$, and return the resulting distances and predecessor edges. If it fails…
nodes.title: Shortest paths in a DAG with a topology check

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted edges on $n$ vertices, $s$ a source, and $\sigma$ a topological order of the directed graph $G$ obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights. For every vertex $t$, the one-pass relaxation from $s$ in the order $\sigma$ leaves the distance of $t$ infinite if and only if $t$ is not reachable from $s$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Infinite DAG distances are exactly unreachable vertices

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted edges on $n$ vertices, $s$ a source, and $\sigma$ a topological order of the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights. If the one-pass relaxation from $s$ in the order $\sigma$ gives a vertex $t$ the finite distance $d$, then $d \le w(p)$ for every path $p$ from $s$ to $t$ made of edge occurrences of $E$, where $w(p)$ is the sum of the weights of the edges of $p$.
nodes.title: Finite DAG distances are at most every path weight

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted edges on $n$ vertices, $s$ a source, and $\sigma$ a topological order of the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights. If the one-pass relaxation from $s$ in the order $\sigma$ gives a vertex $t$ the finite distance $d$, then there is a path from $s$ to $t$ made of edge occurrences of $E$ whose edge weights sum to $d$.
nodes.title: Finite DAG distances are path weights

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted edges on $n$ vertices, $s$ a source, and $\sigma$ a topological order of the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights. In the cost of the one-pass relaxation from $s$ in the order $\sigma$, the number of distance installations is at most the number of edge relaxations.
nodes.title: Distance updates are bounded by edge relaxations

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted edges on $n$ vertices, $s$ a source, and $\sigma$ a topological order of the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights. In the cost of the one-pass relaxation from $s$ in the order $\sigma$, the number of edge relaxations equals the length of $E$, with identical duplicate edges counted separately.
nodes.title: Edge relaxation count of the DAG pass

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted edges on $n$ vertices, $s$ a source, and $\sigma$ a topological order of the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights. If the one-pass relaxation from $s$ in the order $\sigma$ gives a vertex $t \ne s$ a finite distance, then it records a predecessor edge for $t$.
nodes.title: Finite non-source vertices have predecessors

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edge occurrences on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $s$ be a source vertex, and let $\sigma$ be a topological order of the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights. If the one-pass DAG shortest-path relaxation of $E$ from $s$ in the order $\sigma$ ends with an infinite distance estimate at a vertex $v$, then it records no predecessor edge for $v$.
nodes.title: Unreached vertices have no DAG shortest-path predecessor

nodes.title: Predecessor edges of the DAG shortest-path pass

The one-pass DAG shortest-path relaxation of $E$ from $s$ in the order $\sigma$ ends with distance estimate $0$ at $s$.
nodes.title: The DAG shortest-path pass gives the source distance zero

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edge occurrences on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $s$ be a source vertex, and let $\sigma$ be a topological order of the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights. The one-pass DAG shortest-path relaxation of $E$ from $s$ in the order $\sigma$ records no predecessor edge for $s$.
nodes.title: The source has no DAG shortest-path predecessor

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edge occurrences on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $s$ be a source vertex, and let $\sigma$ be a topological order of the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights. The result of the one-pass DAG shortest-path relaxation of $E$ from $s$ in the order $\sigma$ records $s$ as its source.
nodes.title: The DAG shortest-path pass keeps its source

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edge occurrences on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $s$ be a source vertex, and let $\sigma$ be a topological order of the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights. The one-pass DAG shortest-path relaxation of $E$ from $s$ in the order $\sigma$ is charged exactly $n$ vertex visits.
nodes.title: The DAG shortest-path pass is charged one vertex visit per vertex
